facts.claim: Brown et al. (2020) showed GPT-3, a model of 175 billion learned numbers, doing new tasks from a few worked examples placed in the prompt, with no further training.

Zhao et al. (2021) found that the examples in a prompt, and their order, can swing a model’s accuracy from near chance to near the best results, because it leans towards answers it saw near the end or saw often.
Liu et al. (2023) found that models use information best near the start or the end of a long input, and noticeably worse in the middle.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked 2026-10-30) says to treat the model as a brilliant but new employee who lacks your context: the more precisely you explain what you want, the better the result.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked 2026-10-30) calls examples one of the most reliable ways to steer a reply’s format, tone and structure, and suggests three to five of them.
Anthropic’s prompting guide (checked 2026-10-30) says to put long documents near the top and the question at the end, which improved reply quality by up to 30% in its tests.

OpenAI’s prompt engineering guide (checked 2026-10-30) advises marking a prompt’s sections with Markdown or XML tags, giving examples of inputs with the outputs you want, pinning live apps to one fixed model version, and building tests that measure how a prompt behaves.
NVIDIA’s model card (checked 2026-10-30) gives Nemotron 3 Ultra 550 billion learned numbers in all, of which it uses 55 billion for each token.
OpenAI’s model card (checked 2026-10-30) gives gpt-oss-20b, its smaller open model, about 21 billion learned numbers, of which it uses 3.6 billion for each token.
Wei et al. (2021) trained a model of 137 billion learned numbers further on over 60 tasks written as instructions; it then beat GPT-3, given no examples, on 20 of 25 new tasks.
OpenAI’s structured outputs guide (checked 2026-10-30) says its JSON mode makes sure a reply is valid JSON, but only structured outputs make sure it follows the exact shape you supplied.
Anthropic’s pricing page (checked 2026-10-30) charges $2 per million input tokens for Claude Sonnet 5.5, so every token of a prompt is paid for on every request.
